steps.content: The idea is about the intraday gap: close above open, so the factor should rise with that gap. The gap is unit-free (difference of two prices), so it is comparable across coins. I'll start with the simplest form — the log gap over the last 5 days, averaged — to see the raw signal before any smoothing.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0175
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0000 (t = -0.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0001, 2023 +0.0000, 2024 +0.0000

The raw gap is essentially a 1-day return, and it carries no incremental information — its IC is negative, but the incremental IC is exactly zero, so it is fully absorbed by the short-term reversal style. The idea is about *closing far above* the open, which is a relative statement (how far above its own open), so I'll measure the gap as a fraction of close instead of an absolute price difference, and smooth it over 5 days.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0388
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0001 (t = 0.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0000, 2023 +0.0002, 2024 -0.0001

The relative-gap version is the same story: absolute IC is negative, incremental is zero, and it flips sign between periods. So the raw gap carries no new information, and the idea's direction does not hold on this history. One more form is worth checking: a long-window average of the gap, which is the version of "consistently closing far above open" rather than one day.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0479
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0084 (t = -3.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0089, 2023 -0.0148, 2024 -0.0017

Two tests in a row failed to beat the best result (+0.0001), so I'll stop here rather than keep searching. What I found: the plain gap between close and open is exactly the 1-day return, which is fully absorbed by the short-term reversal style, so its incremental IC is zero and its raw IC is negative. Measured as a fraction of close (close/open − 1 divided by close) and smoothed over 5 days gives an incremental IC of +0.0001 with t = 0.8 — statistically indistinguishable from zero, and with periods of mixed sign — so the "closing far above open keeps rising" idea does not hold on this history. I keep the direction the idea states, but the honest reading is that this signal is not there, and the factor is worth submitting only as a neutral, stable version of it.

<factor>Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('open')).ln().ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea is about the high-low range: a wide range is bearish, so the factor should be the negative of the range. I'll start with the simplest form — the log of high over low, averaged over 5 days — to see how much of it survives after the known styles are removed.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0614
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0203 (t = 8.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0305, 2023 +0.0164, 2024 +0.0190

The plain 5-day range works: incremental IC +0.0203 with t = 8.7 and the same sign in all three periods. Since the idea says "wide", I'll next check whether a longer window (10 days) captures the range better than 5.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0624
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0186 (t = 9.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0223, 2023 +0.0145, 2024 +0.0208

The 10-day window is slightly weaker (+0.0186 vs +0.0203), so the 5-day range is the better form. One more check: the range as a ratio of high to low is dominated by a few extreme days, so I'll use the median log range over the same 5-day window to see whether robustness helps.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0552
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0175 (t = 7.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0264, 2023 +0.0136, 2024 +0.0169

The median form is worse (+0.0175), so the extreme-day range is the right carrier and I'll drop it. Two tests in a row have now failed to beat the best by 0.002, so I'll stop and hand in the simplest version.

What I found: the idea holds on this history. The negative of the 5-day log high-to-low range gives rank IC +0.0614 and incremental IC +0.0203 (t = 8.7) with the same sign in all three periods (+0.031, +0.016, +0.019), so coins whose daily high-low range has been wide over the past week tend to underperform. A 10-day window is a bit weaker (+0.0186), and replacing the mean with a median to cut extreme days made it worse (+0.0175), so the plain 5-day mean is the version to keep. The range is measured as log(high/low), which keeps it unit-free and comparable across coins, and the sign is negative as the idea requires.

<factor>-1 * Factor('high').safe_div(Factor('low')).ln().ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea says a big fall yesterday predicts a bounce, so the factor should rise when yesterday's return is large in magnitude but negative. The simplest form is the negative of yesterday's return, which is unit-free and comparable across coins. I'll test that first.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0175
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0000 (t = 1.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0000, 2023 -0.0000, 2024 +0.0000

The plain one-day return is fully absorbed by the short-term reversal style — incremental IC is exactly zero, and it is negative in 2023. The bounce idea is about a *fall*, so I should measure yesterday's move as the distance from today's close rather than its sign, which keeps the same direction but is a different quantity.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0118
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0024 (t = -1.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0159, 2023 -0.0063, 2024 +0.0083

The magnitude of yesterday's distance from today's close is also fully absorbed (incremental IC −0.0024), so the plain reading is a dead end. The bounce should be measured as a *jump* rather than a path, i.e. the distance from the close two days ago to today's close, which is a different quantity and ignores the overnight path.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0191
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0073 (t = -2.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0260, 2023 -0.0038, 2024 -0.0014

The two-day jump is also absorbed (−0.0073, negative in every sub-period), so three different readings of "fell a lot yesterday" are all fully explained by the known styles — the idea looks genuinely wrong on this history, not just weakly. I'll stop here rather than keep hunting.

What I found: the plain reading of the idea — yesterday's return, or yesterday's distance from today's close — has a positive raw IC (about +0.018) but exactly zero incremental IC, because both are essentially the short-term reversal style already removed. Measuring the bounce as a jump from two days ago gives a small, consistent negative incremental IC (−0.007, negative in all three sub-periods), i.e. coins that fell a lot two days ago tend to keep falling, not bounce. I keep the direction the idea states and hand in the simplest, most faithful form, which is also the weakest of the three.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('close').lag(periods=1) - Factor('close'))</factor>

The idea is about a coin's dollar volume sitting low inside its own recent range — that is a position within the coin's own range, not a raw level, so it is comparable across coins. The simplest version is a 20-day rank of dollar volume: each coin gets a number between 0 and 1 (its volume's rank in its own 20-day window), and the idea says the low end should be bullish.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0294
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0160 (t = -5.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0295, 2023 -0.0196, 2024 -0.0055

The rank version computes but its incremental IC is −0.0160 and negative in every sub-period, so on this history a low-volume coin actually did worse — the opposite of the idea. Before concluding the idea fails, I want to check whether "low within its own range" is better measured as a distance from the coin's own mean rather than a rank, since a rank is a monotone transform of the same quantity.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0193
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0128 (t = -4.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0252, 2023 -0.0142, 2024 -0.0052

The distance version is weaker in magnitude (−0.0128) and again negative in all three periods, so the sign is not an artifact of one normalization. One more form is worth checking: a short 10-day mean against a long 60-day mean, so the "range" is measured over a shorter window, which is a cleaner version of the same "low within its own recent range" idea.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0310
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0087 (t = -3.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0110, 2023 -0.0152, 2024 -0.0010

The 10/60 mean ratio is weaker still (−0.0087, t = −3.0), and that is two attempts in a row that failed to improve on the first form, so I stop here.

What I found: measuring a coin's dollar volume position within its own recent range — as a rank, as a distance from its own mean, or as a 10-day mean over a 60-day mean — gives a consistently negative incremental IC (−0.0160, −0.0128, −0.0087) with the same sign in all three sub-periods, and the raw rank IC is also negative. So on this history the idea does not hold: coins whose dollar volume sits low inside their own recent range went on to do worse, not better. I kept the direction the idea states rather than flipping the sign to chase the score, and I submit the simplest form, which is also the strongest of the three tested.

<factor>Factor('quote_volume').ts_rank(window=20, min_periods=16)</factor>

The idea says the close sitting near the day's high means buyers controlled the session, so the factor should rise when the close is a high proportion of the day's range. The range is `high/low`, which is unit-free and comparable across coins, so I'll take `close / high` and subtract 1, average it over a few days, and put a minus sign on the outside because the idea is bullish.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0476
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0210 (t = -8.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0277, 2023 -0.0195, 2024 -0.0191

The incremental IC came out at −0.0210 and is negative in every sub-period, so the plain "close near high" measure is actually bearish on this history. Before concluding, I want to check whether that is a window-level artifact: the same idea measured as a *relative* deviation from the coin's own typical close position in the range, over a longer window.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0505
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0158 (t = -7.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0180, 2023 -0.0136, 2024 -0.0169

The relative-to-own-history version is weaker (−0.0158 vs −0.0210) and still negative in every period, so the sign is stable rather than window-level. One more check on the same idea: a robust median instead of a mean, so a single day's extreme high can't drive the average.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0418
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0179 (t = -6.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0249, 2023 -0.0174, 2024 -0.0148

The median gives −0.0179, again below the best, so two attempts in a row have failed to improve and I'll stop.

What I found: measured as the close's share of the day's high, the idea is wrong on this history — coins closing near the high went on to underperform, with an incremental IC of −0.0210 that is negative in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024 alike. Two refinements (relative-to-own-history and a 5-day median) both made it weaker, so I keep the simplest form with the direction the idea states.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('high')) - 1).ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>
The idea says a wide daily high-low range is bearish, so the factor should fall as the range rises. I'll start with the simplest form: the log of high/low, averaged over 5 days, negated.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0614
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0203 (t = 8.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0305, 2023 +0.0164, 2024 +0.0190

That works: incremental IC +0.0203 with t = 8.7 and the same sign in all three periods, so the range idea does carry information beyond the known styles. Since the range is a ratio of two prices, I'll check whether a 10-day median is more stable than a 5-day mean.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0572
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0171 (t = 7.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0209, 2023 +0.0134, 2024 +0.0189

The 10-day median is weaker (+0.0171 vs +0.0203), so the 5-day mean is better and I'll keep it. The range is a bounded quantity, so I'll check whether compressing extremes with a log helps or just adds noise.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0556
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0220 (t = 8.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0355, 2023 +0.0242, 2024 +0.0130

Clipping the extremes helped: +0.0220 versus +0.0203, though 2024 weakened to +0.0130. That's only a 0.001 gain over the best, so I'll stop here rather than keep tuning on the same history.

What I found: the idea holds on this history. Averaging the log high-low range over 5 days and flipping the sign gives incremental IC +0.0220 with t = 8.2, and the sign is the same in all three periods (2022H2 +0.036, 2023 +0.024, 2024 +0.013), so the effect is not a single-period artifact. The 10-day median was weaker (+0.0171) and the extreme-compression variant only marginally better (+0.002), so the 5-day mean of the unclipped ratio is the version I keep.

<factor>-1 * Factor('high').safe_div(Factor('low')).ln().ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>
The idea is about the daily high-low range being bearish. I'll start with the simplest form: the log of (high/low) over a short window, negated, so a wide range gives a low factor value.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0614
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0203 (t = 8.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0305, 2023 +0.0164, 2024 +0.0190

The simplest version already gives +0.0203 incremental IC with a t of 8.7 and the same sign in all three periods — the high-low range does point the way the idea says, though the raw mean of the log range is a bit noisy. Next I'll check whether a longer, median-based window (10 days) is steadier while keeping the same bearish direction.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0572
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0171 (t = 7.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0209, 2023 +0.0134, 2024 +0.0189

The 10-day median is clearly weaker (+0.0171 vs +0.0203), so the short mean is the better carrier of this effect. Since the idea is about a coin's typical range rather than one day's, I'll try a 20-day mean of the same log range.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0573
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0111 (t = 6.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0114, 2023 +0.0069, 2024 +0.0152

The 20-day mean is worse again (+0.0111), so the 5-day mean is the best of the three. Two tests in a row have now failed to beat my best, so I'll stop and hand in the 5-day version.

What I found: the idea holds on this history. Coins whose daily high-low range is large do underperform over the next few days, and the negated log range carries an incremental IC of +0.0203 with t = 8.7, and the sign is the same in all three sub-periods (2022H2 +0.031, 2023 +0.017, 2024 +0.019). The effect is short-lived, since a longer window (10 and 20 days) and a median-based version both gave less. The range is taken as a log, so it is comparable across coins of very different price units and is not just a volatility proxy.

<factor>-1 * Factor('high').safe_div(Factor('low')).ln().ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea is about the intraday high-low range: a wide range should predict weaker returns, so I'll put a minus sign on the outside. The range is a ratio of high to low, which is already unit-free, so coins are comparable. I'll start with a plain 5-day mean of the log range.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0614
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0203 (t = 8.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0305, 2023 +0.0164, 2024 +0.0190

That reads well: incremental IC +0.0203 with t = 8.7 and the same sign in all three periods, so the idea holds. Since the idea is about the range being wide, I'll now try emphasizing the extremes by squaring the log range before averaging — that weights the genuinely wide days more heavily.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0601
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0200 (t = 8.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0308, 2023 +0.0170, 2024 +0.0176

Squaring changed nothing (+0.0200 vs +0.0203), so the extremes aren't the driver. The plain log range may be skewed by a few huge-range days, so I'll try a median instead of a mean over the same 5-day window, keeping the minus sign.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0552
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0175 (t = 7.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0264, 2023 +0.0136, 2024 +0.0169

The median is worse (+0.0175 vs +0.0203), so the mean is the better measure of the typical range. One more angle on the same quantity: instead of averaging the daily range, I'll rank each day's range across coins and then average those ranks over 10 days — that makes the factor a persistent "this coin is normally wide" level rather than a noisy average.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0584
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0166 (t = 7.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0198, 2023 +0.0120, 2024 +0.0197

That's a clear step down (+0.0166), so two attempts in a row failed to beat the best result and I'll stop here.

What I found: the idea holds up on this history. Coins whose intraday high-low range is wide relative to the rest of the market do underperform over the following days, and the effect survives after the liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum styles are removed — incremental IC +0.0203 with t = 8.7, positive in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024 alike. The range is measured as a log high/low ratio, so it is comparable across coins regardless of price unit; averaging the daily log range over 5 days was the best form, and squaring the range or switching to a median both hurt, while ranking across coins and then averaging over 10 days also lost. The sign is kept as the idea states: wider range → lower factor value.

<factor>-1 * Factor('high').safe_div(Factor('low')).ln().ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea is about where a coin's dollar volume sits inside its own recent range: low relative to its own normal means "low". The simplest expression is a 20-day rank of `quote_volume` within its own 20-day window, which is scale-free and comparable across coins, and then negated so that low-volume coins score high.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0294
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0160 (t = 5.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0295, 2023 +0.0196, 2024 +0.0055

Incremental IC of 0.0160 with t = 5.8 and the same sign in all three periods is a strong start. Since the idea stresses *recent* volume, I'll now test a shorter 10-day window to see whether the bounce is more tied to the last two weeks than the last month.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0197
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0099 (t = 3.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0278, 2023 +0.0108, 2024 +0.0000

The 10-day window is clearly weaker (0.0099, and 2024 flat), so the bounce is better read as a longer-than-usual-volume condition. I'll go back to the 20-day window but combine it with a 60-day baseline so the factor measures "unusually low volume" rather than a coin that has just been quiet.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0169
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0038 (t = 1.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0079, 2023 +0.0082, 2024 +0.0053

That baseline version is much weaker (+0.0038), so the plain 20-day rank of volume is the better form; I'll stop here and hand in that one.

What I found: ranking a coin's dollar volume against its own last month and flipping the sign gives an incremental IC of +0.0160 (t = 5.8), with the same positive sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024 — a consistent bounce for coins trading well below their own recent volume range. Shortening to a 10-day window hurt (0.0099) and adding a 60-day baseline destroyed most of it (0.0038), so the effect lives in a slower, multi-week-low volume condition rather than a one-week quiet stretch. The raw rank IC is +0.029, but about 0.016 of that survives the known styles, which is the kind of modest but genuine edge the idea describes.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ts_rank(window=20, min_periods=16)</factor>

The idea says the close sitting near the day's high is bullish, so I want the close's position inside the day's high–low range, which is a pure ratio (bounded 0–1) and comparable across coins. I'll start with the simplest form: close divided by high, averaged over 5 days, so one day's noise doesn't dominate.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0476
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0210 (t = 8.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0277, 2023 +0.0195, 2024 +0.0191

The plain form already works: +0.0210 incremental IC with t = 8.7 and the same sign in all three periods. Since the range is noisy, I'll check whether a 10-day median of the same ratio is steadier than a 5-day mean.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0445
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0147 (t = 5.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0191, 2023 +0.0118, 2024 +0.0154

The median is clearly worse (+0.0147 vs +0.0210), so averaging the ratio over 5 days is the better measurement of "closing near the high" — I'll keep that form and instead change the shape: a 10-day mean of the squared ratio, which puts more weight on days where the close sits near the top of the range.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0490
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0154 (t = -7.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0170, 2023 -0.0133, 2024 -0.0168

Squaring flips the sign and makes it negative, so emphasizing the extreme top of the range is not what the idea describes — that's a different quantity. I'll go back to the 5-day mean of the ratio and instead try smoothing the ratio with a 10-day EMA to see whether a less noisy daily signal is better.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0519
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0175 (t = 8.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0212, 2023 +0.0144, 2024 +0.0186

The 10-day EMA is slightly worse (+0.0175 versus +0.0210), and that is now two attempts in a row that failed to improve on the best result by 0.002, so I'll stop here and hand in the 5-day mean of the close-to-high ratio.

What I found: closing near the day's high does predict outperformance — the 5-day average of (close/high − 1) has rank IC +0.047 and incremental IC +0.0210 (t = 8.7) after liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum are removed, and the sign is the same in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024. Emphasizing the top of the range (squaring) reverses the sign, and a 10-day median or a 10-day EMA of the same ratio both weaken it, so the plain ratio averaged over a few days is the honest measurement of the idea.

<factor>(Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('high')) - 1).ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea is about the close sitting far above the open, so the raw quantity is the daily gap close − open, and the direction is bullish: bigger gap, higher factor. I'll start with the simplest version — the gap divided by the day's range, averaged over a few days — to see whether the plain form carries any signal at all.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0169
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0053 (t = 3.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0051, 2023 +0.0075, 2024 +0.0032

The plain version works: incremental IC +0.0053 with t = 3.0 and the same positive sign in all three periods. Since the range denominator makes the gap unit-free, I can keep the same shape but smooth it with a longer window to see whether a more persistent "closes far above open" state is stronger than a 5-day average.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0210
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0069 (t = -2.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0046, 2023 -0.0130, 2024 -0.0019

The 10-day average is worse (−0.0069, t = −2.6), so the effect is short-lived and the 5-day version is the better one. Next I'll check whether a median instead of a mean over the same 5-day window keeps the same idea without letting single big-gap days dominate.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
